cats.EIN: Beginners, returning to training & older adults

sl.h: Building muscle with a small surplus
b: A moderate surplus provides the best muscle-to-fat ratio
More calories do not build muscle any faster
Recommendation is based on expert knowledge
sl.fd: Bulking phase: 250–500 kcal above your daily requirement is sufficient.

q.q: How large should the daily surplus be during a bulking phase?

BLK-102.u: Gain rate for beginners and intermediate trainees

sl.h: Beginners: gain 0.25–0.5% per week
b: Beginners and intermediate trainees can tolerate a slightly higher surplus
Target: 0.25–0.5% of body weight per week
Approximately 1–2% per month
sl.fd: At 75 kg: a gain of 0.2–0.4 kg per week is a good rate.

q.q: What weekly rate of weight gain is suitable for beginners in a bulking phase?

BLK-103.u: Gain rate for highly advanced trainees

sl.h: Advanced trainees: gain weight more slowly
b: Those who have been training for over 3 years build muscle more slowly
Therefore, a smaller surplus: 5–10%
Otherwise, more will be stored as fat
sl.fd: After years of training: around 0.25% gain per week, no more.

q.q: Why do highly advanced trainees need a smaller calorie surplus?
q.r: Because they build muscle more slowly
w: Because they build more muscle per week

BLK-104.u: Lean bulk vs. dirty bulk (muscle vs. fat gain)

sl.h: A dirty bulk isn’t worth it
kn: surplus: more fat, same amount of muscle
b: A 15% surplus mainly resulted in thicker skin folds
No general benefit for muscle growth
A lean bulk is more efficient
sl.fd: If you’re gaining more than 0.3% per week: slightly reduce your calories.

q.q: What did a 15% surplus achieve compared to 5% in trained individuals?
q.r: Mainly more fat, with no clear muscle benefit

BLK-105.u: Fat gain and loss of performance with too large a surplus

sl.h: Gaining weight too quickly costs you speed
b: Rapid weight gain produced the same amount of muscle, but five times as much fat
Sprint performance got worse
Particularly relevant for runners and hybrid athletes
sl.fd: As a hybrid athlete: only around 0.2% weight gain per week.

q.q: What happened to sprint performance with aggressive weight gain?

BLK-106.u: Contradictory evidence on extreme calorie surpluses

sl.h: Extreme surplus: slightly more muscle, much more fat
b: Some studies show greater muscle gain with very high calorie intakes
This gain comes with much more fat
Short studies with few participants
sl.fd: Surplus over 20%: expect significantly more fat than muscle.

q.q: What is the cost of an extreme calorie surplus?

BLK-107.u: Protein overfeeding during a calorie surplus

sl.h: Extra protein hardly adds fat
b: A surplus made up solely of protein did not increase fat
Over 8 weeks in trained individuals
For muscle growth, 1.6–2.2 g/kg is still enough
sl.fd: Protein covered? Get the rest of the surplus from carbohydrates and fat, they fuel your training.

q.q: What happened with a calorie surplus coming only from very high protein intake?
q.r: No significant increase in fat mass

BLK-108.u: Macronutrient distribution and protein saturation in a surplus

sl.h: On average, more than 1.6 g of protein brings no extra benefit
b: From 1.6 g per kg, the benefit levels off
Upper limit in the data: 2.2 g per kg
Spread across 3–6 meals
sl.fd: Bulking phase: 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kg, spread across 3–6 meals.

q.q: How should protein be distributed during a bulking phase?

BLK-109.u: Initial body fat percentage and calorie partitioning (P-ratio)

sl.h: You don’t need to get super lean first
kn: body fat for men (20–30% for women)
b: With passive overfeeding, lean people build more muscle
For people who lift, there is no evidence for this
In the healthy range, you can start building straight away
sl.fd: If your body fat is in the normal range: start bulking straight away, no diet needed first.

q.q: Do you need to reach a very low body fat level before a bulking phase?
q.r: No, there is no evidence for this in people who lift
w: Yes, at least 3 months of dieting

BLK-110.u: Impairment of muscle growth due to a calorie deficit

sl.h: No maximum muscle growth in a deficit
b: The deficit slows the gain of lean mass
From around 500 kcal it stops on average
Strength keeps increasing
sl.fd: Goal is maximum muscle growth: don’t stay in a deficit for long periods.

q.q: What works against maximum muscle growth?

sl.h: Building even at maintenance calories
b: Building muscle and losing fat works without a surplus too
Even in trained people
With progressive training and plenty of protein
sl.fd: Don’t want to gain weight: eat at maintenance, plenty of protein, train hard.

q.q: Do you absolutely need a calorie surplus to build muscle?
q.r: No, it’s possible at maintenance with plenty of protein

sl.h: Bulking phases: several months
b: There are no studies on the ideal duration
In practice: 12–24 weeks or longer
Stop when you reach your goal or body fat limit
sl.fd: Plan a bulking phase for at least 3 months – muscles need time.

q.q: What are recommendations on the length of a bulking phase based on?
q.r: On expert consensus and practical experience

BLK-113.u: Transition from a diet to a bulking phase (reverse dieting)

sl.h: Reverse diet: not necessary
b: Raising calories slowly is no better than doing it straight away
Go straight to maintenance after the diet
Hormones need 2–5 months to fully recover
sl.fd: Diet over? Set calories straight to your new maintenance level.

q.q: Is gradual reverse dieting better than going straight to maintenance?
q.r: There is no evidence for that

BLK-114.u: Transition from bulking to dieting (maintenance phase and mini-cuts)

sl.h: Mini-cuts: experience instead of studies
kn: body weight per week while dieting
b: Maintenance phases between bulking and dieting have not been studied
Neither have short mini-cuts during a bulk
The deficit can start right away
sl.fd: You can switch straight from bulking to dieting, a break in between is optional.

q.q: How well is the effect of mini-cuts supported?

BLK-115.u: Intermittent maintenance phases (diet breaks) between phases

sl.h: Diet breaks: only when hungry
b: One-week breaks gave no benefit for fat loss or muscle
Resting metabolic rate stayed the same too
Helpful with strong hunger or a drop in performance
sl.fd: Plan diet breaks when hunger or performance call for them, not as a blanket rule.

q.q: When do one-week diet breaks make sense?
q.r: With strong hunger or falling performance

sl.h: HRV-guided: less hard training, still faster
b: Runners trained by HRV with fewer hard sessions
And improved their 3000 m more
If HRV is outside the normal range, you get easy sessions
sl.fd: Morning HRV clearly lower than usual: go easy today instead of intervals.

q.q: What did HRV-guided runners achieve compared with a fixed plan?
q.r: Fewer hard sessions with bigger improvement over 3000 m

sl.h: HRV guidance and VO2max: no agreement
b: HRV guidance improves vagal HRV
For VO2max the results are contradictory
Beginners and amateurs benefit most
sl.fd: Want to train by HRV: take at least 3 morning measurements per week and use the 7-day average.

q.q: What do meta-analyses say about a VO2max benefit from HRV guidance?

sl.h: In strength training, HRV guidance brings nothing
kn: no benefit for strength or muscle
b: Choosing training days by HRV gave no benefit
Neither for strength nor for muscle mass
A fixed weekly plan is enough
sl.fd: For strength training: stick to your plan, not the HRV number.

q.q: Does HRV-guided strength training bring more strength or muscle?
q.r: No, no benefit over a fixed plan

LOD-104.u: Resting heart rate as a fatigue marker

sl.h: Resting heart rate alone says little
b: Resting heart rate is barely linked to training load
Unsuitable as the only fatigue marker
Always combine it with how you feel and other values
sl.fd: Resting heart rate a bit higher? No reason to panic – check how you feel.

q.q: Is resting heart rate alone a good fatigue marker?
q.r: No, the link is very weak

LOD-105.u: Resting heart rate and autonomic heart rate regulation

sl.h: High HRV isn’t always good
b: HRV rises with good adaptation
But it also rises with overload
Without how you feel, the number is ambiguous
sl.fd: HRV rising sharply, but you feel drained? That can be overload.

q.q: Why can a rising HRV be ambiguous?
q.r: It rises with good adaptation and also with overload

sl.h: Warm-up heart rate as a fitness check
b: Heart rate on the same warm-up run drops as fitness improves
But it also drops with acute fatigue
Studied in elite players
sl.fd: Same warm-up run, clearly lower heart rate and you feel tired: plan some recovery.

q.q: When does heart rate drop during a standardised warm-up?
q.r: With better fitness and also with acute fatigue

sl.h: Session RPE: simple and accurate
b: Effort 0–10 times minutes gives the training load
Matches heart rate-based methods very well
Ask 15–30 minutes after training
sl.fd: 87 minutes at RPE 4 give 348 load points. That is exactly what the app calculates.

q.q: How is training load calculated with the session RPE method?
q.r: Perceived effort (0–10) times duration in minutes

sl.h: Always equally hard makes you ill
b: Monotonous weeks without easy days increase monotony
High monotony and strain went along with more infections
Alternating hard and easy protects you

q.q: What lowers training monotony?

q.q: From which ACWR is the load considered risky?

Weekly load and weekly change are enough

q.q: What is the problem with the ACWR?

w: It is too easy to calculate

sl.h: At the start, the ACWR is useless
b: Different weekly distributions give the same ACWR
In the first weeks it is heavily distorted
Also during taper phases

q.q: Why does the app show the ACWR only after a few weeks?
q.r: Because it is heavily distorted in the first weeks
w: Because only pros are entitled to it
Because it then becomes a paid feature

sl.h: How you feel matters most

Consistent with acute and chronic load

sl.fd: Readiness in the app weights how you feel more than measured values.

q.q: According to the review, what reacts most sensitively to training load?

sl.h: Good questions instead of quick clicks
b: Validated questionnaires are reliable and sensitive to change
Single questions on soreness or mood are barely linked to load
Clear scales matter
sl.fd: Answer the check-in honestly and always at the same time of day.

q.q: How well are unvalidated single questions linked to training load?

sl.h: Overload shows up in the 7-day average
kn: average instead of a single reading
b: With overload, average HRV rose while performance fell
One measurement per week misses this
Daily measurements make it visible
sl.fd: Always use the 7-day average for HRV, not today’s value.

q.q: How can functional overreaching be detected via HRV?
q.r: Via the 7-day average while performance is falling
w: Via a single measurement per week

LOD-115.u: Overtraining and functional overreaching (diagnosis by exclusion)

sl.h: Overtraining: a case for the doctor
b: No single blood value separates overload from overtraining
The diagnosis requires ruling out other causes
What matters is how long recovery takes
sl.fd: Performance drop despite 2–3 weeks of rest: get it checked by a doctor.

q.q: Can a single biomarker reliably detect overtraining?
q.r: No, it needs a medical diagnosis by exclusion

LOD-116.u: Sleep as a steering factor (acute sleep loss and time of day)

sl.h: Less than 6 hours of sleep costs performance
b: Sleep loss lowers performance across the board
The longer you are awake, the worse it gets
Stronger in the afternoon than in the morning
sl.fd: Short night? Move hard sessions to the morning or to tomorrow.

q.q: When is the performance drop after sleep loss larger?

NRG-101.u: Accuracy of formulas (Mifflin-St Jeor vs. Harris-Benedict)

sl.h: Mifflin-St Jeor estimates best
b: The formula estimates resting metabolic rate more accurately than Harris-Benedict
Also with overweight
When no measured body fat percentage is available
sl.fd: The app uses Mifflin-St Jeor as a starting value and adjusts it with your weight trend.

q.q: Which formula estimates resting metabolic rate most reliably in normal adults?

sl.h: For athletes: Ten-Haaf
b: In athletes, Mifflin-St Jeor is clearly off
Ten-Haaf is the most accurate
Studied in over 1,400 athletes

q.q: Which formula is most precise for athletes?

NRG-103.u: Accuracy of formulas in strength athletes (Katch-McArdle & Tinsley)

sl.h: Muscular people underestimate their expenditure
b: Classic formulas underestimate resting metabolic rate in strength athletes
Special formulas using lean mass are more accurate
Only with a reliable body fat measurement
sl.fd: Very muscular and body fat known? Then a formula based on lean mass is more accurate.

q.q: What happens with classic formulas in very muscular athletes?

NRG-104.u: Accuracy of fitness watches for calorie expenditure (overview)

sl.h: Fitness watches guess your expenditure
b: Trackers underestimate energy expenditure on average
The spread is huge
Especially inaccurate when cycling

q.q: How accurately do fitness watches estimate calorie expenditure?

NRG-105.u: Accuracy of fitness watches (heart rate vs. calorie expenditure)

sl.h: Heart rate yes, calories no
b: Watches measure heart rate very accurately when cycling
They miss calorie expenditure by 20–90%
Good for heart rate zones, not for calories
sl.fd: Use your watch for heart rate zones. Treat the calorie value only as a rough guide.

q.q: What are fitness watches reliable for?

NRG-106.u: Weight fluctuations and trend weight (weekly and holiday rhythms)

sl.h: Heavier on Mondays, lighter on Fridays
b: Weight is highest on Sundays and Mondays
Lowest on Fridays
Christmas: +1.35%, often not fully reversed

q.q: On which days is body weight typically highest?

NRG-107.u: Weight fluctuations during the menstrual cycle

sl.h: Your cycle moves the scale
kn: of your period: most water retention
b: Water retention is highest on the first day of the period
Lowest in the mid-follicular phase
Regardless of ovulation

q.q: When is water retention highest in the cycle?
q.r: On the first day of the period

NRG-108.u: Underestimating calorie intake when tracking (diet resistance)

b: Stalled despite supposedly under 1200 kcal: metabolism was normal
Food intake was heavily underestimated

q.q: Why didn’t people lose weight despite a reported 1000 kcal?
q.r: They clearly underestimated their food intake
w: They had too much muscle mass

b: On average, athletes underestimate their intake by a fifth
Compared with a lab method

q.q: By how much do athletes underestimate their energy intake on average?

NRG-110.u: Self-weighing and adherence (effectiveness for weight loss)

sl.h: Weighing only works with a plan
kn: more loss with weighing plus a programme
b: Weighing alone achieved hardly anything
Clearly more weight loss with a behaviour programme
The number needs a response

q.q: When does regular weighing help with weight loss?
q.r: When combined with a behaviour programme

NRG-111.u: Self-weighing and adherence (weighing gaps & loss of adherence)

sl.h: Weighing gaps are a warning sign

Gaps of 30 days or more went along with weight gain
Data from almost 10,000 smart-scale users

q.q: What went along with weighing gaps of 30 days or more?

sl.h: Weighing can be stressful
b: No negative effect in supervised programmes
Without support, especially in younger people, slightly negative
Self-esteem and stress can suffer

q.q: When did self-weighing show no negative psychological effects?
w: With daily weighing without any support

NRG-113.u: Flexible vs. rigid dietary control (long-term success & cognition)

sl.h: Flexible beats strict
kn: rigid control and fixation on body shape
b: Flexible dietary control predicts better long-term success
Strict rules fixate your thoughts on food and body
A slip-up is not a failure
sl.fd: Over your target? No drama – the weekly average is what counts.

q.q: Which dietary control predicts better long-term success?

NRG-114.u: Flexible vs. rigid dietary control (measurement issues & contradictions)

sl.h: Flexible and strict are hard to measure
b: Old questionnaires barely separate the two forms
Both were linked to disordered eating
Feelings like guilt and worry matter too
sl.fd: What matters is not only what you eat but how you feel about it.

q.q: What is a problem with classic questionnaires on dietary control?
q.r: They don’t separate flexible and rigid control well enough

NRG-115.u: Hunger and satiety (short- vs. long-term effects of protein)

sl.h: Protein fills you up – in the short term
b: Protein lowers hunger and the hunger hormone ghrelin
And raises satiety hormones
Long term, the effect on appetite is not certain
sl.fd: Hungry after eating? Have 20–30 g of protein with every main meal.

q.q: How does protein affect the hunger hormone ghrelin?

NRG-116.u: Hunger and satiety (energy density of food)

sl.h: Lots of volume, few calories
kn: calories after eating a whole apple first
b: Foods with low energy density lower body weight
Water 0, carbs and protein 4, fat 9 kcal per gram
Vegetables, fruit and soups fill the stomach
sl.fd: Very hungry in a deficit: eat vegetables, fruit or a soup first.

q.q: How many calories are in 1 g of fat?

NRG-117.u: Keeping weight off after a diet (metabolic adaptation & activity volume)

sl.h: Metabolism barely slows after a diet
kn: lower resting metabolic rate per day
b: The adaptation after a moderate diet is small
It does not predict weight regain
The often-quoted 250 min of exercise per week is not well supported
sl.fd: Goal reached? Recalculate your needs with your new weight – no reason to panic.

q.q: On average, how much does resting metabolic rate drop after a moderate diet?

HYB-101.u: Performance demands in Hyrox and fitness racing

sl.h: Hyrox is mainly a running race
b: You spend most of the time running
Almost the whole race in the hard heart rate range
The highest lactate at the stations, especially the wall balls
sl.fd: Plan about 55–60% of your Hyrox preparation as running and endurance training.

q.q: Where do Hyrox athletes in the Open format spend most of their time?

HYB-102.u: Performance demands in Hyrox and fitness racing

sl.h: Running makes up half the time
kn: share of running in total time
b: Over 39,000 results from 7 seasons
Running decides your ranking the most
Strength stations cost slower athletes disproportionately more time

q.q: How big is the share of running in total time in Pro and Elite races?

HYB-103.u: Performance demands in Hyrox and fitness racing

sl.h: Even pacing wins
b: The elite got faster in every area
Running pace over the 8 rounds became more even
Biggest gains: last run, wall balls, sled pull, farmers carry

q.q: How should you approach the first Hyrox runs?

w: Twice as fast as the rest

HYB-104.u: Performance demands in Hyrox and fitness racing

Mainly knees, lower legs and Achilles tendon
Shoulder injuries are rare

q.q: Which body parts are most often affected in Hyrox athletes?
q.r: Knees and lower legs or the Achilles tendon

sl.h: Endurance decides, not grip strength
b: A faster time goes with a higher VO2max
And with more endurance volume and less body fat
Grip strength and muscle mass showed no link

q.q: What was most strongly linked to a faster Hyrox time in recreational athletes?

b: The stations have fixed heavy loads
Besides endurance, strength endurance and maximum strength count

q.q: Why does maximum strength matter in Hyrox even though it is an endurance race?
q.r: Because the stations have fixed heavy loads
w: Because you can choose your own weights

Sometimes for several days
Don’t put key runs right after leg training

q.q: How long can heavy strength training worsen running economy?

sl.h: Running after stations: practical experience
b: There are no training studies on run-station transitions yet
Recommendations are based on expert knowledge
Typical: 4–6 rounds of a station plus a 400–1000 m run

q.q: How many controlled studies exist on compromised running training?

sl.h: Strength and cardio get along – with a gap
b: Muscle growth and maximum strength don’t suffer
Explosive power is blunted when both happen in one session
With a 3-hour gap the drawback disappears

q.q: What does combined training in the same session mainly blunt?

kn: leg strength in trained people, same session
b: In trained people, cardio in the same session clearly slows leg strength gains
With more than 2 hours apart, clearly less
Beginners are not affected

q.q: When does cardio slow leg strength in trained people the most?
q.r: In the same session with less than 20 minutes rest

b: Less than 6 hours between strength and HIIT reduces both adaptations
6 hours is the minimum
24 hours is optimal
sl.fd: Strength in the morning, HIIT in the evening? Plan at least 6 hours in between.

q.q: What minimum gap between strength and HIIT on the same day does this study recommend?

sl.h: Combined? Strength first
b: Strength before endurance gives more leg strength
VO2max and muscle growth stay the same
Exception: targeted running after stations
sl.fd: Short on time and both in one session: always strength first.

q.q: In which order should you do strength and endurance in one session?

b: After strength training, falling asleep took almost three times as long
After endurance, time awake during the night was longer
Small study with 8 athletes

q.q: What lengthened the time to fall asleep the most in Hyrox athletes?

sl.h: 2-week taper before the race
b: Cut volume clearly, keep intensity and frequency
On average that brings 2–3% more performance
Duration: about 14 days
sl.fd: 14 days before the race: almost halve the volume, keep pace and training days.

q.q: What stays the same during a taper?

b: Fill glycogen stores before intense races
Drink 400–600 ml 4 hours before
Keep fluid loss below 2% of body weight

q.q: How many carbs are recommended the day before a race under 90 minutes?

b: Caffeine boosts endurance and strength endurance
Sodium bicarbonate helps with hard efforts of 30 s to 12 min
Test tolerance in training beforehand

q.q: What must you do before using baking soda in a race?

A single dose on race day does nothing

q.q: What does a single dose of beta-alanine on race day bring?

No difference between pill days and break days
Many studies of moderate quality

q.q: How does performance differ between pill days and break days?

Results on muscle growth are contradictory
Anti-androgenic progestins sometimes showed less growth

q.q: How does the pill affect strength gains from strength training?

b: In the early follicular phase, performance is minimally lower
On average the difference is trivial
78 studies analysed

q.q: How much is performance reduced in the early follicular phase on average?

sl.h: Cycle syncing brings no extra muscle
b: Training strictly by cycle phase is not superior
A consistent programme works just as well
Adjusting by how you feel is still fine

Especially during and just before their period
Performance depends on how you feel, not directly on hormone levels

At least 3 days per week

q.q: Does moderate training in an uncomplicated pregnancy raise the risk of miscarriage?

b: Training clearly lowers gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia

3+ sessions of 25+ minutes

q.q: Which risk does training during pregnancy clearly lower?

Without incontinence or a feeling of heaviness

Most stable after one year

7–12 reps are typical
